text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me alright? I'm Tracey, nice to meet you.
B: Yeah, I can hear you. I'm Shazia.
A: Shazia, lovely. Where are you calling from, hun?
B: Blackburn.
A: Oh, up north! I'm Chelmsford, Essex. Sat in my kitchen, as you can probably tell. Did you do that puzzle thing at the start? Because I'll be honest, I rushed it. I'm not a sit-still-and-think person, I just wanted to get it done, you know?
B: Erm, yeah. I did it. Some of them were hard.
A: The shapes ones, weren't they? I just guessed half of them to be fair. So what do you do then, are you working?
B: No. Not at the minute.
A: Oh right, fair enough.
B: I was in a warehouse. Packing, nights. Had to stop because of my back.
A: Oh, nights are brutal. And packing, all that bending and lifting, it kills your lower back, honestly I see it all the time. I'm a fitness instructor, I do PT as well, and half my over-fifties come to me with backs that have just gone from years of lifting stuff wrong. Have you had any physio or anything?
B: GP sent me swimming. Women's session.
A: Oh, swimming's brilliant for backs. Did it help?
B: I went three times.
A: Three times! Babe, that's not long enough to tell, you've got to give it a couple of months, yeah?
B: I know. It weren't for me, the swimming. Too early, and the changing rooms were freezing.
A: No, I get it, I get it. Sorry, I'm going into trainer mode, my son says I do it to everyone. He's seventeen, Callum, doing his A-levels. Leaves his washing on the floor, drives me mad. Have you got kids?
B: No.
A: Oh, okay.
B: Just me and my husband. My mum's round the corner, I'm there most days.
A: Oh, that's nice, being close. I don't see my mum enough to be honest, since my dad passed. She's still in Basildon and with the A12 traffic it's a nightmare getting over there. I should go more. What's he do then, your husband?
B: He drives a taxi.
A: Oh, he must have some stories, I bet! Late nights though.
B: Fridays and Saturdays, yeah. He's out till three, four.
A: So what do you do with yourself evenings when he's out? Feet up, telly?
B: Erm, I watch dramas. Pakistani ones on YouTube.
A: Oh, are they good? I'm the same with Netflix, all the true crime stuff. And The Traitors, did you watch The Traitors?
B: No. I don't really watch English stuff. The dramas, they go on for ages, like forty episodes. There's one now with a mother-in-law who's horrible to the girl, honest, I shout at the screen.
A: Ha! Oh, I love that. That's me with Gogglebox. So you cook as well, I bet, proper home cooking?
B: Yeah. Saalan, daal, chapatis. Every day nearly.
A: See, I'm rubbish at all that. I meal prep on a Sunday, chicken, rice, boxes in the fridge. Very boring. Then at the weekend I go out for an Italian and undo it all with Prosecco.
B: Mine's not healthy. Imran likes it hot, lots of oil.
A: Well, it's what you enjoy, isn't it? Life's too short. Do you get out for walks with your back, or is that bad as well?
B: Bit. To my mum's and the shop.
A: Even that's something, honestly, walking's the best thing you can do. I do Parkrun a couple of times a month, I did the London Marathon once, and I swear it's...
